title: fix(plugin-security): the position refusal reads no retired catalog table and names the catalog type it judged against; the unimported per-organization catalog module is deleted
body:
Fixes #15196
Part of #15204
Clause-②: no

## What this does

This is the last item of #15196 and stage 6c of #15204, in one PR. Both parts remove residue the retired security catalog left behind, and both do it by deletion. That follows the cutover batch rule (6094179271): only delete, never fix the retired modules.

1. **`position-catalog-refusal.ts`.** The id-to-name hint (`idSpellingHints`) read `sys_position`, which is not registered on `main`. The hint is deleted, together with its record-id read context and the hint form of the message. The refusal envelope's `constraint.target` also named that retired table. It now names `position`, the security catalog type the value is judged against.
2. **`position-catalog-refusal.test.ts`.** The suite no longer boots `sys_position`, `sys_permission_set` and `sys_position_permission_set` from the legacy testkit. It now boots the way production does.
3. **`per-organization-catalog.ts` and its test are deleted.** The module had 28 lines, one export and no importers.
4. **`scripts/check-logger-receiver-detach.mjs`.** The gate's must-not-fire control had a provenance comment naming the deleted file. It now names a live file that uses the same spelling.
5. A patch changeset: `.changeset/15196-retired-catalog-residue.md`.

Landing point: the file surface of claims 6251403239 and 6251408540. Nothing outside it changed.

## Measurements

These were taken on `origin/main` `dd72a047`, in this branch's worktree.

**M1: the hint never fires in production. Confirmed.**
- No non-test code declares or registers `sys_position`. `git grep "name: 'sys_position'"` finds 0 hits outside tests (control: `name: 'sys_user_position'` finds its object file). `git grep '\bSysPosition\b'` finds 0 hits outside tests and testkits.
- I ran a real `ObjectQL` engine over `SqlDriver` with no `sys_position` registered. `find('sys_position', …)` throws `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` (404). The control, `find` on a registered object, answers `[]`. The hint's `catch` swallowed that throw, so it never returned a hint.
- Behavioural proof, commit `35a9404c`: with the suite moved off the legacy testkit and the source still unchanged, all 25 cases pass. The two record-id cases already read the generic remedy, so the hint was absent before any source change.
- The verdict reads only the security catalog: `securityCatalogReaderOf` reads the registry, then the metadata service, and never a row. Apart from the `sys_user_position` pre-image, the hint was the module's only row read.

**M2: readers of this refusal's `constraint.target`. None outside its own suite.**
- objectstack: there is no non-test reader of `constraint.target` or `constraint?.target`. The only two hits are this suite's own pins. The refusal builds its message itself rather than through `renderValidationMessage`, whose six callers are other refusals. So no `{{target}}` template ever renders this value.
- objectui (`/home/user/objectui` at `43efd07`): `git grep` over `*.ts` and `*.tsx` for `constraint.target`, `constraint?.target` and `.constraint` readers finds one hit. It is a TypeScript AST `typeParameter.constraint` in a guard test, unrelated to field errors. The field-error consumers read `code` and `message` only: `plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx` switches on `code`, and `AssignedUsersSection` shows `message`. No renderer and no i18n key reads `'sys_position'` from a refusal.
- **Choice: `target: 'position'`**, with `targetField: 'name'` unchanged. `position` is the security catalog type the refusal resolves the value against (`POSITION_CATALOG_TYPE`). Reasons:
  - it names what the value was actually judged against;
  - the sibling refusal on `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set` (`grant-permission-set-name.ts`) already sends `target: 'permission'`, pinned in its suite, so both catalog-reference refusals now use the same form.
  The engine's lookup refusal puts an object name in `target` because a lookup points at an object. This column points at a catalog type.
- **Published surface: neither narrowed nor widened.**
  - No schema changes: `FieldErrorSchema.constraint` stays an open record.
  - No accept set changes: the same values are accepted and refused as before.
  - One runtime value changes: `fields[].constraint.target` goes from `sys_position` to `position`. I found no reader of it in either repo, and the changeset states the new value.
  - `POSITION_CATALOG_OBJECT` and `idSpellingHints` were exported from an internal module only. Neither was in the package's `index.ts`.

**M3: `per-organization-catalog.ts` has no importer. Confirmed.**
- `rowMatchesDeclaration` has one hit: its own definition.
- `per-organization-catalog` appears in no import specifier. The remaining hits are prose: ADR-0131, the `plugin-sharing` comment covered under M4, and the gate's control comment.
- Positive control for the grep spelling: it finds the `import … namesWithoutCatalogRow` line in the refusal suite.

**M4: stale pointers.**
- `scripts/check-logger-receiver-detach.mjs:503` named the deleted file as the place the `logger?.error?.(message)` spelling was measured. It now names `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/member-role-canonical.ts`, which uses that spelling at `:481` and is on no retirement list.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/bootstrap-declared-sharing-rules.ts:47` is left as it is: C3 stage 9 (#23952, in flight) retires that file, and the claim excludes it.

## Test deletion: case 6 of `per-organization-catalog.test.ts`

Case 6 never imported the module it was filed under. It pinned `resolveUserAuthzGrants` from `@objectstack/core`, reached through core's `dist/`, against `sys_position` and junction rows booted from the legacy testkit. Core's own resolver suites pin each of its assertions, importing the resolver from its source:

| Case 6 assertion | Duplicate (same function, in its own package, imported from source) |
|---|---|
| A member of the other organization does not collect the binding organization's junction set | `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.test.ts` › §6a › "a member removed from alpha: the definition's set and nothing alpha bound — with no tenant and in beta" |
| The binding organization's own member does not collect it either | Same describe › "a current alpha member gets the same: alpha's organization-scoped junction rows bind nothing" |
| Positive control: the set the `everyone` definition names reaches both members | Both cases above assert exactly `['global_everyone_default']`; also `resolve-authz-context.grant-set-by-name.test.ts` › "the `everyone` definition's set resolves; a junction row binding another set confers nothing" |
| Why the cross-organization leak cannot come back | `resolve-authz-context.grant-set-by-name.test.ts` › "the junction, the id bridge and the catalog rows are never read". The resolver reads none of `sys_position`, `sys_position_permission_set` or `sys_permission_set`. |

Run here: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/security/resolve-authz-context.test.ts src/security/resolve-authz-context.grant-set-by-name.test.ts`. Result: 2 files and 120 tests passed, including all four named cases.

Case 6 used a real driver to pin how the engine's scope and the driver's predicate combined during a `sys_position` sweep. The resolver no longer reads that table (the last row above), so there is nothing of that kind left to pin.

No case of `position-catalog-refusal.test.ts` was deleted: it had 25 cases before and has 25 after. The hint assertions changed along with the behaviour they pinned, and now expect the generic remedy. The walled case that used a name only one organization's row carried now compares two names the catalog does not hold. The walled record-id case gained one assertion: it reads no `sys_position`.

## Reverse verification

This was a one-shot check at `7427cac5`, run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. For each leg the anchor hit exactly once and the file's blob hash changed. After each leg the restore was proven: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The suite imports the subject by relative source path (`./security-plugin.js`), so there is no `dist/` step.
- **Leg 1:** `constraint.target` set back to `'sys_position'`. Result: 2 failed, 23 passed. The failures are exactly the two `constraint` pins (`- "target": "position"` / `+ "target": "sys_position"`).
- **Leg 2:** the swallowed `sys_position` record-id read planted back before the throw. Result: 1 failed, 24 passed. The failure is the walled record-id case: `expected [ 'sys_position', 'sys_position' ] to not include 'sys_position'`.

## Tests and gates (at `2fb7b362`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (the package's `test` script is `vitest run`): 187 files passed; 3736 tests passed and 45 skipped. Lock VERDICT `command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck`: lock VERDICT `command-exit 0`.
- Before the change, `src/position-catalog-refusal.test.ts` and `src/per-organization-catalog.test.ts` passed 26 of 26. After it, `src/position-catalog-refusal.test.ts` passes 25 of 25.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths) derived 88 families. I ran all 88 at `2fb7b362` after a full `turbo run build` and recorded each exit code before any pipe: all 88 exited 0.
- `--ran` reconciliation: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 88 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 88 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED`.
- `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` ran detached, as its header asks, and exited 0.
- `--ran` also flagged that `origin/main` moved 6 commits during the run (to `c4526a70`). None of those commits touches `plugin-security` or any file in this diff. CI runs the merge ref.
- Changed lines: 436 (87 added, 349 deleted) across 6 files, under the 3,000-line threshold.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:4317` still says the refusal fires when a position "names no `sys_position` catalog row". In fact the verdict reads the security catalog. That file is outside this claim's file surface, so I did not edit it. Carrier: none.
- Row 23b of `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` still mentions "a name only a `sys_position` row carries". That is still true of rows left in an existing database, so I left it.
- Lines 44–49 of the `position-catalog-refusal.ts` module doc describe the verdict against leftover `sys_position` rows. They are still accurate, so I left them.
